description: Post-Harvey Houston-Galveston Roadway Bridge Reconnaissance is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Jamie Padgett, Rice University (rice.edu). Hurricane Harvey made a landfall on August 25, 2017 near Port Aransas, Texas, as a category 4 hurricane. Harris County experienced 33.7 inch (856 mm) of rain during a four day period, resulting in significant flooding, prompting controlled releases of surrounding reservoirs, and affecting transportation infrastructure across the region. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/DS2HM4H. Keywords: Hurricane Harvey, Reconnaissance, Houston, Galveston, Roadway bridge, Flooding. Published 2018-05-17. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated in the DesignSafe listing (publication licences offered are CC BY 4.0, ODC-By, CC0 and GPL; project page not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
